summary: Spain's Interior Ministry says entry for stays of up to 90 days in any 180-day period is governed by the Schengen Borders Code. EU nationals travel freely with a passport or ID card; nationals of the countries on the EU's visa-exempt list need no visa (the ETIAS travel authorisation is not yet in operation), and others need a Schengen short-stay visa costing EUR 90.

defaultStayWindow.text: 90 days in any rolling 180-day period, counted across the whole Schengen Area rather than per country. Leaving and coming back does not reset the allowance: the Schengen Borders Code counts the 180-day period preceding each day of stay, so days already spent anywhere in the area during that period still count against the 90. The Schengen Borders Code counts the date of entry as the first day of stay and the date of exit as the last.

source.name: Schengen Borders Code (Regulation (EU) 2016/399), consolidated text — EUR-Lex
source.instrument: Regulation (EU) 2016/399 (Schengen Borders Code), Article 6(1) — no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, considering the 180-day period preceding each day of stay; Article 6(2) — date of entry is the first day of stay, date of exit the last

fee.notes: Children 6–11: EUR 45; under 6: free (EU Visa Code). Spain's Order AUC/891/2024 says the EUR 90 fee for A and C visas has applied since 11 June 2024.

processing.text: That period may be extended up to a maximum of 45 calendar days in individual cases, notably when further scrutiny of the application is needed.

stayDays.text: This Regulation establishes the procedures and conditions for issuing visas for intended stays on the territory of the Member States not exceeding 90 days in any 180-day period.

extendable.text: The period of validity and/or the duration of stay of an issued visa shall be extended where the competent authority of a Member State considers that a visa holder has provided proof of force majeure or humanitarian reasons preventing him from leaving the territory of the Member States before the expiry of the period of validity of or the duration of stay authorised by the visa.

method.text: An application shall be examined and decided on by the consulate of the competent Member State in whose jurisdiction the applicant legally resides.

applyWindow.text: The EU Visa Code says an application is lodged no more than six months before the start of the visit and, as a rule, no later than 15 calendar days before it; in justified urgent cases the consulate may accept it later.

fee.notes: The Visa Code fee: EUR 90, EUR 45 for children aged 6 to 11, and nothing for children under 6. The EU–Russia visa facilitation agreement has been suspended in whole for Russian citizens since 12 September 2022 (Council Decision (EU) 2022/1500). The European Commission said on 7 November 2025 that Russian nationals will no longer be able to receive multiple-entry visas and will have to apply for a new visa each time they plan to travel to the EU, with exceptions for limited and justified cases such as independent journalists and human rights defenders.

tips.text: The UK government says visits to Schengen countries in the 180 days before you travel count towards your 90 days, so time spent in other Schengen countries counts against the same allowance as Spain.

The UK Foreign Office says that under the EU's Entry/Exit System you may be asked to give biometric details every time you enter or exit the Schengen area, and that the checks can take extra time, so allow more time at the border.
ETIAS is not in operation yet, and no applications are being collected. The EU's official ETIAS website is travel-europe.europa.eu.
Canada's travel advice says pickpocketing and bag snatching are common, especially in Madrid and Barcelona, and that thieves often target tourists at weekends, holidays and festivals.

faq.question: Do US citizens need a visa for Spain?
faq.answer: No. The United States is on the EU's list of countries whose nationals are exempt from the visa requirement for stays of no more than 90 days in any 180-day period. Once ETIAS starts, visa-exempt travellers will need this travel authorisation (EUR 20 application fee) to enter.

faq.question: How much does a Spain Schengen visa cost?
faq.answer: The EU Visa Code sets the Schengen short-stay visa fee at EUR 90 for adults and EUR 45 for children aged 6 to 11. Spain's Interior Ministry says short stays are of up to 90 days in any 180-day period.

faq.question: Is ETIAS required to enter Spain?
faq.answer: ETIAS is not yet in operation, and no applications are being collected; the EU will announce the start date several months before launch. The EU says the application fee will be EUR 20 (applicants under 18 or over 70 are exempt from paying) and that an authorisation is valid for three years or until your passport expires, whichever comes first.

faq.question: Is travel insurance mandatory for Spain?
faq.answer: The EU Visa Code requires it of Schengen visa applicants: travel medical insurance with minimum cover of EUR 30,000, valid throughout the Schengen states for the whole intended stay.

faq.question: How long can I stay in Spain without a visa?
faq.answer: Nationals of the countries on the EU's visa-exempt list can stay no more than 90 days in any 180-day period, and Spain's Interior Ministry applies the same 90-in-180 limit to short stays in Spain.
